items.raw_excerpt:

Instead of generating a modal from patterns, why not fetch the actual UntitledUI modal? How it works:
- AI says "add a settings modal"
- MCP fetches the real component + all base dependencies (buttons, inputs, etc.)
- Files are placed in your project with correct imports Tools available:
- search_components: Find by name/description
- get_component_with_deps: Fetch with all dependencies
- get_example: Fetch complete page templates (dashboards, landing pages) Requires UntitledUI Pro license for premium components. Base components are free. GitHub: https://git

items.title: Sentinel – Zero-trust governance for AI Agents
items.raw_excerpt: Hi HN, I’m a software engineer and I’ve been building agentic workflows lately. Like many of you, I got concerned about giving LLMs "write access" to tools. Whether it's a payment API, a database deletion, or a simple email send, the risk of a hallucination causing a $5k mistake is real. I wanted a way to keep a human in the loop without rewriting my entire agent logic every time. So I built Sentinel. It’s a lightweight Python layer that wraps any tool/function. The key principles I focused on: Fail-secure by default: If the rules engine or the network fails, the action is blocked. Most systems fail-open, which is a nightmare for security. items.title: InsAIts V2 – Real-time monitoring for multi-agent AI communication
items.raw_excerpt:
Hi HN,
I'm Cristian, an indie developer from Italy working on tools to make multi-agent AI safer and more debuggable.
When agents talk to each other (CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, custom setups), they quickly develop shorthand, lose context, invent jargon, and propagate hallucinations — all invisible to us.
InsAIts is a lightweight Python SDK that adds observability in ~3 lines of code.
V2 just shipped with: Anchor-aware detection (set the user's original query as context to reduce false positives)
Forensic root-cause tracing + ASCII chain visualization
Built-in domain dictionaries (finance, healthcare, kubernetes, ML, devops, quantum)
Local (Ollama) decipher mode — translates agent jargon to human-readable (Cloud soon)
Integrations: Slack alerts, Notion/Airtable export, LangGraph/CrewAI wra

Author | Zhao Zhiqi  Editor | Bao Yonggang  
Before the first snow of January fell in Beijing, we met Professor Zhai Jidong at Tsinghua University. Holding a thermal cup, he spoke briskly, with almost no pauses or ambiguities even while thinking and narrating simultaneously.  
This tenured professor from Tsinghua’s Department of Computer Science, who has led his team to win 15 world supercomputing championships, was dissecting an industry anomaly:  
Why, amid the soaring parameters of large models and the declining cost of computing power, are users’ burdens for AI implementation growing heavier?  
He pointed out that high scores on benchmarks may not always align with users’ actual needs. Sometimes, the same model can perform vastly differently across various MaaS platforms, as some providers apply "castration-level" quantization to reduce costs. Faced with a dizzying array of MaaS suppliers, users must weigh performance, price, and stability, often exhausting their energy just by surveying market quotes.  
"Leaving the initiative of model selection entirely to users is actually a significant challenge," Zhai Jidong stated frankly. This "paradox of choice" not only torments developers but also erodes corporate profits. For enterprises, the core of cost reduction and efficiency improvement may not lie in pursuing the most cutting-edge models, but in how to deploy appropriately capable models—using expensive large models for complex tasks and lightweight small models for routine ones.  
Recognizing this pain point, Qingcheng Jizhi, an AI infrastructure startup founded by several of Zhai Jidong’s former students, developed an intelligent routing system.

Este profesor titular del Departamento de Informática de Tsinghua, que ha liderado al equipo para ganar 15 campeonatos mundiales de supercomputación, estaba desentrañando una peculiaridad de la industria: ¿Por qué, en un momento en que los parámetros de los grandes modelos se disparan y los precios de la potencia de cálculo bajan, la carga de implementación de IA para los usuarios es cada vez mayor? excerpt_i18n.en: In 2025, China's smart glasses market is experiencing pre-breakout turbulence. Data from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shows that shipments in the first three quarters exceeded 1.78 million units, representing a several-fold increase compared to 2024. The annual sales of 2 million units for Meta Ray-Ban's camera glasses validate the market's potential. Companies like Xiaomi and Li Auto are entering the fray, but the industry is mired in a collective dilemma: consumers are forced to choose among audio, camera, and display glasses, with newly purchased devices quickly becoming obsolete due to rapid technological iteration. Manufacturers are obsessed with a lightweight race but are trapped in the impossible triangle of "lightweight, strong performance, and long battery life." Just as the entire industry is caught in a cycle of "innovation for innovation's sake," Xuanjing unveiled a potential breakthrough at its Tech Open Day. Its M6 series breaks the boundaries of product form with a "magnetic modular" design, redefines user experience logic through "active AI interaction," and challenges the industry's decade-old iron law of iteration with the concept of "one purchase, perpetual upgrades." Modularity rewrites the rules of iteration. Users don't want three functionally fragmented glasses but a solution that can be combined and upgraded as needed, said Xie Xin, Vice President of Xuanjing, capturing the original intent of modular design. In April 2025, Xuanjing launched the ultra-lightweight 25.8-gram M5 clip-on AR glasses, whose "zero-barrier" design compatible with prescription glasses topped three major JD.com charts within four hours of release, further solidifying the team's commitment to modularity.
excerpt_i18n.es: En 2025, el mercado chino de gafas inteligentes experimenta una agitación previa a su explosión: datos del Ministerio de Industria y Tecnología de la Información muestran que las ventas en los primeros tres trimestres superaron los 1,78 millones de unidades, multiplicándose varias veces en comparación con 2024. Las gafas con cámara Meta Ray-Ban, con ventas anuales de 2 millones de unidades, confirman el potencial del mercado. Fabricantes como Xiaomi y Li Auto se han sumado al sector, pero la industria se enfrenta a un dilema colectivo: los consumidores se ven obligados a elegir entre gafas de audio, de cámara o con pantalla, y los dispositivos recién adquiridos pronto quedan obsoletos debido a la rápida innovación tecnológica, convirtiéndose en "chatarra electrónica". Los fabricantes, obsesionados con la competencia por la ligereza, caen en el trilema imposible de "ligereza, alto rendimiento y larga duración de la batería". Mientras toda la industria se debate en la "innovación por innovar".

items.raw_excerpt: 当大模型的能力从能回答问题走向能完成任务，AI for Science 也正在经历一次更深层的转向。 过去行业更关注模型在标准题目、知识问答和文献总结上的表现，但这些能力本质上仍属于信息处理，它们可以提升效率，却很难真正改变科研本身的推进方式。 现实科研的核心难点并不在于单点能力是否强，而在于研究过程天然是长链条、不确定、强依赖验证的闭环系统。一个看似简单的物理问题，往往需要经历建模选择、推导路径、数值实验设计、代码实现、调参排错、对照基准结果、误差来源分析等一整套流程，任何一步出错都可能导致结论失效。 也正因为如此，科研效率的瓶颈长期不在想法是否聪明，而在能否把想法变成可信结果，大量时间消耗在重复工程与试错迭代中。 在这样的行业背景下，上海交通大学 SciMaster 团队联合深势科技、中科院理论物理所在研究论文《PHYSMASTER: Building an Autonomous AI Physicist for Theoretical and Computational Physics Research》中给出了一个更激进的答案，与其把 AI 当作分散的辅助工具，不如直接构建一个能够组织、规划并执行科研闭环的自主系统。 研究团队用五个真实的物理科研任务验证其能力，从加速成熟工作流，到自动完成复杂数值研究，再到尝试自主探索开放问题，展示了 AI 迈向可持续推进科研的可能路径。 这项研究真正值得关注的地方，不只是模型算得更快或写得更像人，而是它让我们看到一种潜在的新科研范式，AI 不再只是科研流程中的局部工具，而可能成为能够承担完整研究链条的研究主体之一。 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19799 五项任务跑通科研闭环 这项工作并不是在一个统一的数据集上跑模型分数，而是通过五个真实的物理科研任务来验证系统能力，并将这些任务按能力层级分为三

excerpt_i18n.en: As large models evolve from answering questions to completing tasks, AI for Science is undergoing a deeper transformation. Previously, the industry focused more on model performance in standardized tasks, knowledge Q&A, and literature summarization, but these capabilities essentially remain forms of information processing. While they can enhance efficiency, they hardly alter the fundamental approach to scientific research. The core challenge in real-world research lies not in the strength of isolated capabilities, but in the inherently long-chain, uncertain, and validation-dependent closed-loop nature of the research process. A seemingly simple physics problem often requires a full workflow: model selection, derivation pathways, numerical experiment design, code implementation, parameter tuning and debugging, benchmarking against reference results, and error source analysis. Any misstep can invalidate the conclusions. Consequently, the bottleneck in research efficiency has long been not the cleverness of ideas, but the ability to transform ideas into credible results, with significant time spent on repetitive engineering and trial-and-error iterations. excerpt_i18n.es: Cuando las capacidades de los grandes modelos evolucionan de responder preguntas a completar tareas, la IA para la Ciencia también está experimentando una transformación más profunda. Anteriormente, la industria se centraba más en el rendimiento de los modelos en preguntas estándar, respuestas de conocimiento y resúmenes de literatura, pero estas habilidades pertenecen esencialmente al procesamiento de información; pueden mejorar la eficiencia, pero difícilmente cambian verdaderamente la forma en que avanza la investigación científica. La dificultad central de la investigación real no radica en si una habilidad puntual es fuerte, sino en que el proceso de investigación es inherentemente un sistema cerrado de cadena larga, incierto y fuertemente dependiente de la verificación. Un problema físico aparentemente simple a menudo requiere pasar por la selección de modelos, la ruta de derivación, el diseño de experimentos numéricos, la implementación de código, el ajuste de parámetros y la depuración de errores, y la comparación.
